protocol_type: Two-wire synchronous serial bus with software addressing; no opcode/command set

channels.name: SDA
channels.description: Serial data line; open-drain (or push-pull in UFm); pulled HIGH by Rp; carries address byte + data bytes + ACK/NACK.

channels.name: SCL
channels.direction: master output (slave input; slave may pull LOW to stretch)
channels.description: Serial clock line; open-drain; pulled HIGH by Rp; 9 clock pulses per byte (8 data + 1 ACK).

valid_ready_handshake_rules: Per-byte handshake: receiver pulls SDA LOW during the 9th SCL clock pulse to ACK; leaves HIGH to NACK.
Optional clock-stretching handshake: slave holds SCL LOW after a byte to delay the next byte.
There is no AMBA-style per-cycle VALID/READY; the handshake is byte-level + bit-level via SCL synchronization.

transaction_framing.start_S: HIGH-to-LOW transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH
transaction_framing.stop_P: LOW-to-HIGH transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH
transaction_framing.repeated_start_Sr: Functionally identical to S; keeps bus busy without an intervening STOP
transaction_framing.byte: 8 data bits + 1 ACK clock pulse = 9 SCL cycles
transaction_framing.ack_bit: Receiver pulls SDA LOW during 9th SCL clock pulse
transaction_framing.nack_bit: SDA remains HIGH during 9th SCL clock pulse

address_byte_format.bits_0_to_7: 7-bit slave address (LSB-first into ADDRESS field, MSB-first on wire)
address_byte_format.bit_8: R/W direction bit; 0 = write to slave; 1 = read from slave
address_byte_format.10_bit_addressing: Two address bytes: first byte 0b11110XX0/1 (XX = upper 2 address bits + R/W); second byte = lower 8 address bits

single_response_for_write: Every byte (including the address byte) is acknowledged by the receiver via an ACK / NACK on the 9th clock pulse.
per_beat_response_for_read: Each read byte gets an ACK from the master-receiver, except the last byte where master sends NACK to signal end of transfer.

rows: Reserved for future purposes including Device ID

master_to_slave_write_transaction: S → SLAVE_ADDR[7:1] || R/W=0 → ACK → DATA0 → ACK → DATA1 → ACK → … → P
Optional repeated START between bytes: S … DATA → ACK → Sr → SLAVE_ADDR2 || R/W → …
slave_to_master_read_transaction: S → SLAVE_ADDR[7:1] || R/W=1 → ACK (slave) → DATA0 (slave drives SDA) → ACK (master) → DATA1 → ACK → … → DATAN → NACK (master) → P
